sources: recreation.gov campsite catalog for facility 261780 (31 sites), read 2026-10-28

values.note: 29 individual sites plus two group sites. 'Many sites are designed for tent or van camping. Large camp trailers are accommodated best in pull-through campsites 5, 7, 11'; sites 1-16 take longer trailers. recreation.gov lists 15-45 ft for most sites and 75-90 ft for 5-9 (11 is listed at 99 ft, a placeholder-looking figure). Up to 2 vehicles and 8 people a site.

sites.source: https://www.blm.gov/visit/sand-gulch-campground ('Sand Gulch campground has 29 individual sites, two group sites, and two vault toilets. Individual sites are limited to 2 vehicles and 8 people.'; 'Many sites are designed for tent or van camping. Large camp trailers are accommodated best in pull- through campsites 5, 7, 11') + recreation.gov notice ('Sites 1-16 accommodate longer trailer units (5, 7, 11 are pull through sites).') + catalog (Max Vehicle Length 5 and 7 90 ft pull-through, 9 90, 6 85, 8 75, 11 99), read 2026-10-28

values.note: No trash service; bring water and firewood and pack out trash.

facilities.source: https://www.blm.gov/visit/sand-gulch-campground ('two vault toilets'; 'Drinking water, electric hook-ups and trash service are not available at Sand Gulch Campground.'), read 2026-10-28

hookups.source: https://www.blm.gov/visit/sand-gulch-campground ('Drinking water, electric hook-ups and trash service are not available') + recreation.gov notice ('There are no hookup services'), read 2026-10-28

values.note: Open year-round; June-August heat and pinyon gnats can make camping unpleasant (recreation.gov).

season.source: https://www.blm.gov/visit/sand-gulch-campground ('a 31-site camping facility, open year-round') + recreation.gov notice ('During the months of June, July and August, the extreme heat and the presence of pinon gnats, flies, ants and other insects can make camping during these months unpleasant.'), read 2026-10-28

values.note: Sites 1-15 and the group sites are reservation-only (individual sites up to 30 days ahead, groups 3 months), and can be booked the same day; sites 16-29 are first-come, paid at the entrance pay station. Cell coverage is limited, so book before arriving.

booking.source: https://www.recreation.gov/api/camps/campgrounds/261780 (notice: 'Sites 1-15 and Group Sites are Reservation Only, Sites 16-29 are First Come, First Serve, pay at the Pay Station at the entrance. Reservations can be made the day of. Cellphone Coverage is limited'; 'Maximum length of stay is 14 days.'; facility_rules reservationWindow 30 Days, groupReservationWindow 3 Months), read 2026-10-28

values.note: Individual sites $20 a night, group sites $40 (2026-2028 rate tables). An $8 non-refundable reservation fee per reservation.

fees.source: https://www.blm.gov/visit/sand-gulch-campground ('Individual Sites: $20 per night | Group sites: $40 per night | There is an $8 non-refundable reservation fee for each reservation.') + https://www.recreation.gov/api/camps/campgrounds/261780/rates (StandardSite $20, GroupSite $40, 2026-2028), read 2026-10-28

note: BLM (Royal Gorge Field Office) campground in the Shelf Road climbing area, ~14 mi north of Canon City at ~6,400 ft among limestone cliffs and pinyon-juniper: from US-50 take Dozier Ave and Field Ave north onto CR 9 (Shelf Road) about 10 mi. Come from the Canon City end; the upper (Cripple Creek) end of Shelf Road is narrow and steep and not recommended for trailers or motorhomes. --Claude
summary: BLM page + recreation.gov: confirmed $20, no hookups, no water, reservable with first-come sites. Changed count 27->29 (BLM: 29 individual + 2 group), max_rig_ft 99->90 (the 99 on site 11 looks like a placeholder; sites 5, 7, 9 are 90 ft). Added pull-throughs, vault toilets, no trash, water/sewer false, year-round season, 30-day window, 14-night limit, $8 reservation fee, fees checked 2026. Note rewritten.
flags: Phone 719-269-8500 confirmed (BLM Royal Gorge Field Office, BLM page and recreation.gov).

Length: BLM itself gives no figure, only 'Large camp trailers are accommodated best in pull- through campsites 5, 7, 11' and 'Many sites are designed for tent or van camping'. recreation.gov's per-site lengths are mostly 15-45 ft; 5-9 are 75-90 ft and 11 is 99. Set 90, which still overstates every site but those few; EKKO fits sites 1-16 per the notice.

Road: the BLM directions use the Canon City end (CR 9 north ~10 mi). The Gold Belt Byway FAQ (search snippet) says the upper portion of Shelf Road is not recommended for trailers, campers or motor homes (tight curves, narrow spots, steep grades). No 4WD requirement on the Canon City approach in any source read.
recreation.gov's reservationCutOff rule reads '3 / Not Reservable', but its own notice says 'Reservations can be made the day of'; no cutoff recorded.
Pin 38.61737,-105.22956 equals the BLM coordinates; ~85 m from the catalog centroid, ~30 m from the nearest site. OK. Waterfront 'not waterfront' confirmed (dry gulch, no water).
